findings.rationale: Feature distribution shifts from round 10-11 onward (drift mean_shift_sd z=+4.1, onset flagged at round 10; round-11 shift of about 1.07 SD in GenHlth, with a sustained shift of about 0.9 to 1.6 SD afterwards). The shift coincides with a calibration break: CITL was near zero in rounds 3-9 and is about -0.10 from round 11. Final-round CITL is -0.084 (z=-6.2) with ECE z=+4.2, and subgroup O/E is about 2 in both sexes. Updates are anomalous (median norm ratio 2.55, z=+5.0; min cos -0.64). AUC is normal (0.822), so this is not label noise. Feature tails also stand out at round 20. Data change, not a manipulated upload, is the primary explanation.

DiffWalk and GenHlth features shift from round 11 onward and stay shifted (shift_sd about 0.8 to 1.2 every round from 11 to 20), giving mean_shift_sd z=+4.3. Round-20 feature tails are strong outliers: DiffWalk p01 z=-7.2 (z_noise -5.5), GenHlth p99 z=-9.1 (z_noise -6.4), HighBP p01 z=-8.0 (z_noise -6.0). Updates show negative-cos outliers (min cos -0.60, z=-3.1). Local AUC (0.833) and CITL (-0.033) are close to normal, so the fault appears as a feature shift rather than a label or calibration fault.

DiffWalk feature mean shifts by about 1.05 SD at round 11 and stays shifted (mean_shift_sd z=+4.7; onset 11). The same round shows a break in local calibration: CITL is negative from round 11 (final -0.058, z=-4.4). Updates change abruptly at round 11: norm ratio jumps from about 1.1 to 3.5-4.2 and cosine turns negative (about -0.1 to -0.7). Because the feature shift is a data change and local AUC is normal, I attribute the update anomaly to the drifted training data rather than to a manipulated upload. Poisoning is the main alternative, and the update pattern alone would support it, but the local data fault is independently visible. Confidence is moderate.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with update, performance, drift, feature-tail and subgroup views (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed suspects with narrower calls. Budget is fully spent (20.0). Three clients (SC, UT, WI) show a consistent drift signature: a feature-distribution shift from round 10-11 onward, together with update and calibration anomalies. I reported them as drift at moderate confidence. WI's update anomaly (norm ~3.5x, negative cosine from round 11) could also be read as poisoning, but its concurrent local data shift and CITL break favour drift. No label noise (AUCs normal), prevalence-only shift, subgroup bias (O/E is high, not low, in every subgroup), missing-value sentinels, or free-riding was supported by the evidence. Weak leads not reported: GU (small client, mean_cos z=-3.1), DC and MT subgroup cells (small n, |z_noise| about 3-4), and several single feature tails with |z| about 3-5. Those are consistent with noise.
